This male victim went on to correctly identify two men from the truck who were arrested. Surveillance footage shows the reason he was only able to identify two of them, and not all four. The victims are seen walking towards their vehicles to leave the festival when a Chevy pickup truck speeds past them. The victims then stand there confused as the truck circles back around and returns to the parking lot next to them. The driver of the truck parks and exits the vehicle followed by the right back seat passenger who gets out with what looks like a rifle, which he racks, indicating he's ready to open fire. Words are exchanged between the two groups, and then the two men get back inside the truck as they continue yelling at the victims. They then speed off with the other two passengers never being seen, explaining why the victims could only identify two suspects. The four men included a father named Jeffrey, his juvenile son in the seat behind him also named Jeffrey and two of their friends, Uriel, who was in the front passenger seat, and Jose, who was in the back right passenger seat, and also the one carrying the firearm. After obtaining a search warrant, multiple open containers of alcohol were found inside the truck as well as a folded-up dollar bill that tested positive for cocaine, two loaded handguns, and a loaded AR pistol, which very closely resembles a rifle, were also found inside the truck and seized. The juvenile son of the driver as well as Uriel, the man in the front passenger seat had no charges filed against them. Jeffrey, the driver, was charged with felony second-degree assault and felony unlawful possession of a firearm. He took a plea deal, pleading guilty to unlawful possession of a firearm while the assault charge was dropped. He was sentenced to four total days in jail and was released back into the public. Jose, the man who threatened the victims with the firearm, was charged with three counts of felony second-degree assault. He took a plea deal, pleading guilty to all three charges in exchange for a sentence of seven total days in jail and was then released back into the public.
